atlas-vn.0001: English is tested or certified for the better graduate roles: FPT Software’s 2026 fresher post asks for English equivalent to TOEIC 700+, Vietcombank’s outstanding-graduate track asks for IELTS 7.0, TOEIC 785, TOEFL 550 or CEFR C1, and Grant Thornton Hanoi asks for fluent English; in the 2018 British Council survey of 150 employers, 77% of foreign companies and 76% of conglomerates said English skills were particularly important, while Vietnamese remains the language of local firms.
atlas-vn.0002: Graduate programmes in Vietnam recruit mainly from February to June: Viettel opened registration on 12 February 2026 and its trainees started on 11 May, FPT Software’s 2026 fresher post gave a deadline of 3 April, Vietcombank’s wave III closed on 14 June 2026 for posts needing no experience and BIDV’s wave I on 16 June 2026; Grant Thornton Hanoi’s January–March 2026 internship closed on 17 September 2025; Tet fell on 14–22 February 2026 and is followed by a hiring peak for experienced staff until April.
atlas-vn.0003: Unemployment among 15-to-24-year-olds was 8.86% in the first quarter of 2026 (9.04% in the fourth quarter of 2025 and 8.6% for 2025), against 2.23% for all working-age people in the second quarter; about 1.4 million young people, 10.2% of the youth population, were neither working nor in education or training. We found no unemployment rate for graduates alone; VnEconomy reports that around 70% of university graduates still need retraining after entering the workforce.
atlas-vn.0004: Under Decree 219/2025, active students with an internship agreement or job offer are exempt from work permits upon obtaining a certificate, while foreign experts need a degree plus 2 years of experience (1 year in tech and finance). Ho Chi Minh City’s economy grew 8.03% in 2025.
atlas-vn.0006: A fast-growing city economy, with rising credit and foreign investment
atlas-vn.0008: over US$8.1 billion of direct investment in 2025
atlas-vn.0009: Ho Chi Minh City’s jobs and graduate hiring by sector are not given in any source read, so only business is rated, on one company headquarters.
atlas-vn.0010: Vietnam was not covered by the research library before this record.
atlas-vn.0011: Ho Chi Minh City’s economy grew 8.03% in 2025; outstanding credit exceeded VND5 quadrillion (about US$190 billion), up more than 13%, foreign direct investment passed US$8.1 billion, up more than 21%, and the digital economy was about 25% of output.
atlas-vn.0020: Hanoi’s GRDP grew 8.16% in 2025, 16th among Vietnam’s localities, according to the National Statistics Office.
atlas-vn.0021: Hai Phong’s GRDP grew 11.81% in 2025, contributing 8.58% of national growth, according to the National Statistics Office.
atlas-vn.0022: Da Nang’s GRDP grew 9.18% in 2025 to an estimated VND316.1 trillion, ninth among Vietnam’s 34 localities and second among its six centrally run cities.
atlas-vn.0023: Hanoi’s, Da Nang’s and Hai Phong’s ratings rest on one or two named employers or a port statistic, not on jobs by sector.
atlas-vn.0024: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Ho Chi Minh City 67th in the world, up 17 places, and lists Da Nang for the first time, in 71st position.
atlas-vn.0025: FPT Corporation’s headquarters is at 10 Pham Van Bach Street, Cau Giay, Hanoi; it had 54,110 employees in more than 30 countries and territories, and describes a semiconductor R&D centre in Da Nang.
atlas-vn.0026: Techcombank’s head office is Techcombank Tower, 6 Quang Trung Street, Hanoi, and its total workforce reached 12,705 employees at 31 December 2025, up from 11,848 a year earlier.
atlas-vn.0027: Vinamilk’s headquarters is at 10 Tan Trao Street, Tan My Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, and its chief executive thanks nearly 10,000 employees.
atlas-vn.0028: Hai Phong Port handled 2 million TEU for the first time in 2025; cargo through the Hai Phong port area was over 104 million tonnes in the first 11 months, up about 8%, and Hateco Hai Phong International Container Terminal opened in February 2025.
atlas-vn.0029: The pay, output and population metrics are for each city within its boundaries before the mergers of 1 July 2025 (the national statistics office’s 63-province book, 2024; pay is for 2023), so they do not match the merged city areas used in the growth claims above; Vietcombank, VinFast, Viettel and the Ho Chi Minh City banks were not read.
atlas-vn.0030: headquartered in the city; nearly 10,000 employees
atlas-vn.0034: 2 million TEU handled for the first time in 2025
atlas-vn.0035: semiconductor R&D centre in Da Nang
atlas-vn.0036: Vietnam’s big graduate programmes recruit through online applications, tests and interviews, and the competition is heavy: Viettel Talent 2026 drew nearly 12,000 applications. English is asked for in the better roles, and employers in a 2018 survey called Vietnamese-owned firms more hierarchical than foreign ones. Graduates back from abroad without local contacts reported little to lean on.
atlas-vn.0037: No survey ranks the routes in Vietnam; this is first because the large employers found recruit this way, and the competition shows it: Viettel Talent 2026 drew nearly 12,000 applications from 13 countries (about 8,800 to its technical track and nearly 3,000 to its management track), and more than 800 trainees attended its opening on 11 May 2026.
atlas-vn.0038: Techcombank Future Gen is a 24-month rotational programme for final-year students and people with under 2 years of experience, in four tracks (Technology, Digital & Data, Business, General Management); the 2025 edition opened for applications in June 2024.
atlas-vn.0039: Vietcombank recruits branch staff in waves: in wave III of 2026, regular candidates took a professional exam and an interview, while outstanding graduates of six named universities went to interview only. BIDV’s wave I of 2026 had six customer-relationship-manager groups, two of them for foreign-invested clients in Korean or Chinese.
atlas-vn.0041: Grant Thornton Hanoi’s 2026 internship (audit or tax) took final-year students with an average mark of 7.0 or above for at least 3 months from January to March 2026; the deadline was 17 September 2025. The page does not say how many interns are hired.
atlas-vn.0042: Viettel Digital Talent, a technology internship, reports that across the 2021–2025 seasons nearly 1,200 interns were trained and over 400 became Viettel employees while still studying. FPT Software’s fresher programme pays a training allowance for 3 to 6 months with a chance to become full-time.
atlas-vn.0043: HUTECH’s technology exhibition and recruitment day on 7 May 2026 gathered nearly 180 companies offering nearly 7,000 jobs and internships, with students able to apply on the spot. We found no count of how many graduates are hired through fairs.
atlas-vn.0045: VietnamWorks (run by Navigos Group), ITviec for IT jobs and CareerViet (whose banner showed 19,681 openings) are the portals read; VietnamWorks takes one CV per application as .doc, .docx or .pdf under 5,120 KB and cannot be re-applied to.
atlas-vn.0046: For experienced hires, Vietcetera (2021) describes the three months from Tet to April as the best time to recruit because job-seekers have just received their yearly bonus; Vietcombank’s wave III kept experienced posts open until 31 December 2026 or until the quota was filled.
atlas-vn.0047: Times Higher Education, summarising one researcher’s interviews, says most returning undergraduates who had never worked in Vietnam had “no point of leverage”, while postgraduates on government scholarships already had networks. In the British Council survey of 150 employers, 66% agreed that people who studied abroad know the local market less well.
atlas-vn.0048: Adecco Vietnam’s general director, quoted in the British Council report, said clients would love to hire graduates who have spent time overseas for their language skills. We found no count of graduate hires made through agencies.
atlas-vn.0049: Programmes recruit from February to June: Viettel opened registration on 12 February 2026 and its trainees started on 11 May; FPT Software’s 2026 fresher post gave a deadline of 3 April (the page also lists 4 May); Vietcombank’s wave III closed on 14 June 2026 for posts needing no experience and BIDV’s wave I on 16 June 2026.
atlas-vn.0050: Some windows open much earlier: Grant Thornton Hanoi’s deadline for its January–March 2026 internship was 17 September 2025, and Techcombank’s Future Gen opened in June 2024 for its 2025 edition, through September 2024.
atlas-vn.0051: Experienced hiring peaks after Tet (a public holiday from 14 to 22 February 2026), which Vietcetera called a three-month “golden period” until April; its figures are from 2021.
atlas-vn.0052: Vietcombank’s outstanding-graduate track names six universities: National Economics University, Foreign Trade University (Hanoi), Academy of Finance, Banking Academy, Banking University of Ho Chi Minh City and University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City.
atlas-vn.0053: For degrees from abroad, 88% of the 150 employers in the British Council survey agreed that studying overseas adds value, and Adecco Vietnam’s director said clients mostly want good English rather than a particular country. The survey dates from 2018.
atlas-vn.0054: HUTECH Technology Exhibition and Recruitment Day: 7 May 2026, Ho Chi Minh City; nearly 180 companies and nearly 7,000 jobs and internships.
atlas-vn.0055: Viettel Talent 2026 opening: 11 May 2026 at Viettel’s headquarters, for the more than 800 trainees selected; it is not a public fair.
